comparator.name: Fiscale Economie
comparator.sourceNotes: Tilburg’s current official programme and curriculum pages establish a three-year, 180-ECTS Dutch-language bachelor combining economics, business, law and taxation. Years 1 and 2 each contain 60 compulsory ECTS. Year 3 contains a genuine 30-ECTS choice among exchange/study abroad, a 24-ECTS internship plus a 6-ECTS elective, or Economics and Management minors; this open space is preserved rather than instantiated. The remaining 30 ECTS comprise four compulsory 6-ECTS courses and a 6-ECTS bachelor thesis. The table displays the thesis under both semesters because it may start in either semester, while explicitly stating that its total load is 6 ECTS; it is therefore counted once. Zero-credit GROW activities are programme features but are excluded from the 180-ECTS component total. No formal route is selected.
components: Genuine choice among exchange/study abroad, a 24-ECTS internship plus a 6-ECTS elective, or Economics and Management minors.
Compulsory bachelor thesis; students start in semester 1 or semester 2, for a total of 6 ECTS.

candidates.label: Tax policy, justice and social impact

selection.assessment: The closest match owns the programme’s combined fiscal-economics identity, general tax-policy and legislation interests, major tax bases, effects on economic choices, and relationship between economic developments and tax law. Two further generator-backed clusters remain: corporate and multinational taxation with financial/legal analysis supports a business, accounting and finance direction; tax justice, societal tax questions, beneficial fiscal policy and perspective-balancing support a public-policy and social-equity direction. Both are coherent, mechanically feasible and materially distinct while explicitly acknowledging that UCR offers no specialist Dutch tax curriculum. The closest match differs from each related direction by six courses, while the two related directions differ by eleven; all three alternatives are included.

alternatives.label: Economics, taxation & public finance
alternatives.labelReason: The curriculum combines the strongest available UCR economics and public-finance sequence with business, accounting, finance, law, EU institutions and research methods. The label states those available fields and does not imply that UCR offers a specialist fiscal-economics degree.
alternatives.concept: The closest feasible UCR response combines economics, taxation and public-spending analysis with accounting, finance, business and legal foundations, EU and international institutions, empirical research and persuasive communication.
progression: Law, Society & Justice in semester 1 precedes every later course that formally requires it. Research Methods & Statistics precedes all selected economics courses with that prerequisite, while Entrepreneurship & Business Foundations precedes Transnational Business Law, International Business & Governance and Money, Banking & Finance. Introductory economics precedes the advanced economics sequence conceptually. The Art of Rhetorical Communication precedes Rhetoric in Action. The final year concentrates advanced private law, EU politics, governance, econometrics, finance and qualitative research. Every course is available in its assigned term and every formal prerequisite is completed in an earlier semester.

alternatives.label: Business taxation, accounting & finance
alternatives.labelReason: This direction concentrates the available UCR business, accounting, finance, commercial-law, governance and quantitative courses around the fiscal consequences of company decisions. The label does not claim specialist instruction in Dutch corporate taxation.
alternatives.concept: A business-focused response combining economics, accounting, finance, commercial regulation, international business, strategy, organisational behaviour and empirical research to examine how fiscal rules shape firms and investment decisions.
alternatives.distinctness: Compared with the closest match, this route removes criminal law, constitutional and administrative law, EU law, EU politics, international-relations theory and qualitative social research. It adds digital business strategy, organisational leadership, business and regulation in the age of AI, behavioural economics, market research and applied rhetoric. Six of the 24 courses differ, and the organising choice shifts from a broad law-and-public-finance comparison to business organisation, commercial decision-making and finance.
progression: Law, Society & Justice, Entrepreneurship & Business Foundations and Introduction to Economics establish the legal, business and economic strands in semester 1. Research Methods & Statistics precedes all selected courses that formally require it; Entrepreneurship & Business Foundations precedes Strategy & Digital Transformation, Transnational Business Law, International Business & Governance, Money, Banking & Finance and Market Research. The Art of Rhetorical Communication precedes Persuasive Communication. The final year advances from accounting, macroeconomics and organisational leadership to private law, global governance, finance, econometrics, behavioural economics and independent market research. Every course is available in its assigned term and every formal prerequisite is completed in an earlier semester.

alternatives.label: Tax policy, justice & social equity
alternatives.labelReason: This direction uses UCR public economics, behavioural economics, law, politics and sociology to examine tax design, institutions, ethics and fairness. The label signals a policy and social-analysis route, not a specialist tax qualification.
alternatives.concept: A public-policy and social-science response combining taxation and redistribution analysis with behavioural economics, law, political institutions, sociology, ethics and mixed research methods to study fair and effective tax systems.
alternatives.distinctness: Compared with the closest match, this route removes the business-foundations, accounting, international-business, macroeconomics, finance and transnational-business-law courses. It adds sociology, modern and contemporary social theory, political philosophy, peace and conflict, and behavioural economics. Six of the 24 courses differ from the closest match and eleven differ from the business direction. The route is therefore organised around public authority, institutions and society rather than commercial practice.
progression: Law, Society & Justice, Introduction to Economics and Introduction to Sociology establish the legal, economic and social foundations in semester 1. Law, Society & Justice precedes every later law course with that formal prerequisite, and Research Methods & Statistics precedes all selected advanced economics courses. International law, constitutional law and international-relations theory precede the advanced EU-law, EU-politics and conflict courses conceptually. Introductory rhetoric precedes Rhetoric in Action, and introductory sociology precedes advanced contemporary social theory conceptually. The final semester brings together qualitative methodology, econometrics, behavioural economics and applied public communication. Every course is available in its assigned term and every formal prerequisite is completed in an earlier semester.

notes.text: Tilburg’s programme is a specialist fiscal-economics degree combining a continuous sequence in Dutch personal, business, corporate and value-added taxation with economics, accounting, finance, public and private law, European and international tax, formal tax procedure, ethics and a fiscal-economics thesis. UCR can combine public economics and taxation analysis with business, accounting, finance, broad law, politics, sociology and research methods. It does not teach the Dutch tax code, personal and corporate income tax, VAT, formal tax procedure or the programme’s multi-course fiscal sequence. These pathways therefore compare related economic, business, legal and policy fields; none reproduces the external fiscal-economics discipline or its professional preparation.
